fields.rationale: Wishbone B4 is a SoC bus / interconnect protocol, not a peripheral with a control register file. There is no MMIO register map in this document. The protocol carries the integrator-defined SLAVE address on [ADR_O()]. Concrete Wishbone-compliant IP cores define their own register files at the SoC integration level — outside this protocol spec.

ADR_O_width_bits.note: Modular address width — defined per IP core by the higher array boundary; lower boundary determined by data port size and granularity (e.g. on a 32-bit data port with BYTE granularity, [ADR_O(n..2)]).

address_decoding_options: Full address decoding (every SLAVE decodes the entire address bus)
Partial address decoding (SLAVE decodes only the bits it requires) — preferred for Wishbone systems to reduce redundant logic
address_side_field_widths.minimum_subordinate_decode_granularity: Implementation-defined; partial decoding lets the SLAVE pick any contiguous decode window required by the SLAVE's internal address space.
address_side_field_widths.address_tag_TGA_O: User-defined tag attached to [ADR_O()] for purposes such as address-size identification (16-bit / 24-bit / 32-bit), parity, or protected-memory marking. Its semantics MUST be defined in the WISHBONE DATASHEET (RULE 3.70).
address_side_field_widths.data_organization_relationship: The [SEL_O()] array width = port_size / granularity (e.g. 64-bit port with BYTE granularity -> [SEL_O(7..0)]). [SEL_O(n)] qualifies a byte lane of [DAT_I()]/[DAT_O()] per Section 3.5.

fields.notes: If a future system-integration L4 is required for a Wishbone-compliant IP, the canonical 'address-side fields' to capture would be: [ADR_O()] width, [SEL_O()] width = port_size/granularity, [TGA_O()] semantics (per WISHBONE DATASHEET), [SEL_O()] -> byte-lane mapping (BIG / LITTLE ENDIAN per Section 3.5), and (for Registered Feedback) the [CTI_O()] + [BTE_O()] burst tags.

evidence.spec_section: 2.1.1 General Requirements for the WISHBONE DATASHEET
evidence.quote: The WISHBONE DATASHEET MUST indicate the port size. The port size MUST be indicated as: 8-bit, 16-bit, 32-bit or 64-bit.
The WISHBONE DATASHEET MUST indicate the port granularity. The granularity MUST be indicated as: 8-bit, 16-bit, 32-bit or 64-bit.

The address output array [ADR_O()] is used to pass a binary address. The higher array boundary is specific to the address width of the core, and the lower array boundary is determined by the data port size and granularity.

The select output array [SEL_O()] indicates where valid data is expected on the [DAT_I()] signal array during READ cycles, and where it is placed on the [DAT_O()] signal array during WRITE cycles. The array boundaries are determined by the granularity of a port.

Address tag type [TGA_O()] contains information associated with address lines [ADR_O()], and is qualified by signal [STB_O]. For example, address size (24-bit, 32-bit etc.) and memory management (protected vs. unprotected) information can be attached to an address.
WISHBONE supports both full and partial address decoding. Partial decoding is preferred because it reduces redundant logic in the system.
